_meta.purpose: Features of the 13 reference-class importations (data/importation-reference-class.json), coded as known at the index's laboratory confirmation, for the case-conditioned Kenya forecast (lovs/forecast/kenya_conditioned.py). Used to reweight literature priors and for leave-one-out validation against the plain base rates.
_meta.coder_exposure: Coded by the forecast author, who had read every episode's outcome in the reference-class file before coding. Features are taken from the at-detection facts in each episode's notes and sources, not from outcomes, but the coding cannot be blind. This file was committed before any validation score was computed.

fields.e_comm: range of the share of a typical case's community (home, travel, family) transmission that happened in the destination before isolation
fields.e_hosp: range of the share of a typical case's hospital-phase transmission that happened in destination health facilities
fields.f_pre: range of the infectiousness-weighted fraction of the destination hospital phase before Ebola-grade precautions
fields.pre_level: precautions before Ebola-grade care: NONE (unsuspected, no Ebola precautions) or STANDARD (standard, droplet or contact precautions)
fields.post_level: precautions after: STANDARD, VHF (Ebola-grade PPE in an isolation unit) or HLIU (high-level isolation unit)
fields.p_death: judged probability, at detection, that the index dies in the destination
fields.e_fun: range of the share of funeral or body-handling exposure that happened in the destination
fields.funeral_level: TRADITIONAL or SDB (safe and dignified burial, or remains handled by authorities)
fields.responder: index was a returning responder or health worker (Block 11 subgroup)
fields.multi_import: episode merged several imported cases (more transmission opportunities than one index)

episodes.rationale: Returned from the Guinea outbreak area before that outbreak was recognised; ill and cared for in Lofa (home and local facility) with no Ebola precautions; burial practice not stated, coded traditional with a wide range.

Acutely ill on arrival 20 July, taken straight to a private hospital, first treated for presumed malaria, then isolated without Ebola-grade equipment (MMWR 2014;63:867); remains handled by authorities.

Onset about 16 Aug in Dakar while staying with relatives; outpatient care from about 18 Aug; admitted 26 Aug; Ebola recognised only at confirmation 29 Aug; alive on about day 13 of illness at detection.

Onset at home in Dallas; emergency visit 25 Sept unsuspected and discharged; readmitted 28 Sept under standard, droplet and contact precautions; confirmed 30 Sept while critically ill (MMWR 2014;63:1087).
Returning responder, self-monitoring, reported fever and was isolated within hours in a biocontainment unit.
Young child symptomatic during public-transport travel through Mali; admitted to a Kayes facility 20 Oct, unsuspected until sampling 22 Oct; severely ill.
Returning health worker, febrile in transit, isolated the next morning and moved to a high-level isolation unit.
Returning health worker; onset 10 May at home, admitted 11 May, confirmed 12 May, transferred to a high-level isolation unit.
Arrived with her children, fell ill in Monrovia, unsuspected; died 31 March; confirmed post mortem, so burial under protocol.
Sick child crossed with family 10 June into a district on Ebola alert, seen at a facility and moved to an Ebola treatment unit within about a day; confirmed 11 June.
Symptomatic child identified by point-of-entry screening and isolated immediately; body repatriated.
Crossed about 8 May, admitted to a private hospital in Kampala 11 May, unsuspected; died 14 May before confirmation 15 May; body returned to the DRC the same day (handling in Uganda only).
Returning physician self-reported symptoms on arrival and was isolated immediately in a high-containment unit.
